'''''Orbea variegata''''', also known as the '''star flower''', '''carrion flower''',  '''starfish cactus''' and '''toad cactus''',<ref>{{cite web |title=Carrion flower (Orbea variegata) |url=https://weeds.dpi.nsw.gov.au/Weeds/Carrionflower |website=NSW WeedWise| date = 2024 |publisher=NSW Department of Industry|access-date=1 April 2025}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Apocynaceae]] that is native to the coastal belt of the [[Western Cape]], South Africa, growing actively during the winter rainfall season.<ref name="bes">{{cite web |last1=Bester |first1=Stoffel Petrus |title=Orbea Haw. |url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantnop/orbea.htm |website=PlantZAfrica | date = 2006 |publisher=SANBI |access-date=21 September 2016}}</ref> It is an [[invasive species]] in southern [[Australia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pir.sa.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0013/240025/carrion_flower_fsheet.pdf|format=PDF|title=Carrion flower : Orbea variegata|website=Pir.sa.gov.au|access-date=24 March 2022|archive-date=28 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220328231515/https://pir.sa.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0013/240025/carrion_flower_fsheet.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Description==
Growing to {{convert| 10|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert| 50|cm|in|abbr=on}} broad, it is a leafless [[succulent]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] with cactus-like toothed stems, and highly variable, star-shaped, off-white or yellow flowers strongly speckled with maroon, up to {{convert|8 |cm|in|abbr=on}} in diameter. The succulent, stocky or slender shoots lie at the base and then ascend, or stand upright, forming small clumps with a diameter of 5 to 20 cm, rarely up to one meter. The slender [[Shoot (botany)|shoots]] grow to about 15 cm long or high with a diameter of about 0.5 to 1 cm. Stocky shoots only grow to 4 to 5 cm high with a diameter of less than 1 cm. The shoots are green with purple spots. The warts are splayed and up to 3 to 9 mm, rarely up to 1.5 cm long. They are loosely arranged in four obtuse-angled ribs, each with a longitudinal groove between the ribs. The rudiments of [[stipule]]s may be missing. The [[latex]] is colorless.

===Inflorescences===
[[File:Orbea variegata (Csillag virág) (1).jpg|Flower|thumb|left]]
The flowers may show regular (banded) markings, or irregular ones. They have five pointed or blunt lobes surrounding a central, pentagonal annulus (corona).<ref>{{cite web 
| url = http://www.cactus-art.biz/note-book/Dictionary/Dictionary_A/dictionary_annulus.htm
| title = Annulus (botany) | publisher = Cactus-art.biz |  access-date = 15 April 2018}}</ref> The flowers may have a faint [[Carrion flower|carrion smell]] to attract potential insect pollinators.<ref name = EOS>{{cite web 
| url = http://www.llifle.com/Encyclopedia/SUCCULENTS/Family/Asclepiadaceae/19768/Orbea_variegata
| title = ''Orbea variegata'' | publisher = Encyclopedia of Succulents | access-date = 15 April 2018}}</ref> The [[inflorescence]] stem is 2 to 6 mm long and 0.2 to 0.3 mm in diameter. The inflorescence contains one to five flowers. The flower buds are elongated and pointed at the end, but also flat and rounded. The [[hermaphrodite]] flower is radially symmetrical and has five [[petal]]s. The five [[sepal]]s are about 9 mm long. The five petals are fused in a flat, basin-shaped manner, and the corolla has a diameter of 5 to 9 cm. The corolla is green on the outside, and the corolla lobes and [[Leaf|venation]] are tinged with red. The inside of the corolla is pale greenish-yellow or light yellowish with a variable pattern of more or less large blackish-purple, crimson, or purple-brown spots and dots. The round or rounded-pentagonal annulus is usually lighter yellow and more finely patterned. The margin is recurved, the surface warty, and transversely wrinkled on the inside. The corolla tube encloses the [[Perianth|corona]]. Flowering occurs from late summer to early fall.

The petal lobes are approximately triangular, flat-spreading, or slightly curved outwards, with a length of about 2.5 cm and a width of about 2.3 cm. The corona, which measures 6 to 7 mm in diameter, is pale yellow with dark purple dots, or dark purple. The interstaminal coronal lobes are deeply pocket-shaped, oblong-rectangular and up to half bifid or bidentate, as well as ascending and diverging. The staminal coronal lobes are 3 mm long and 1.2 mm wide and ovate-lanceolate in shape. They have thread-thin or subulate processes of approximately equal length at the base and upper end, which project beyond the style head at the upper end. The ends are club-shaped and curved outwards. There is a [[nectar]] cavity, the opening is teardrop-shaped. The [[pollinia]] are narrowly D-shaped, 0.8 mm wide and 0.5 mm high. The [[Follicle (fruit)|follicle]]s are arranged in pairs, at an acute angle to each other, and upright. They are long, spindle-shaped with a smooth surface and up to 12 cm long

==Cultivation==
This plant is popular in cultivation, and is often sold under its former name ''Stapelia variegata''. It has many common names, including starfish plant, starfish cactus, carrion cactus, carrion flower, toad cactus, toad plant.<ref name = EOS/> It is not closely related to the true [[cactus]] family. When grown as an ornamental plant in temperate zones it requires protection, as it does not tolerate freezing temperatures. It is best grown under glass, in similar conditions to cacti.

In the UK it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/120546/i-Orbea-variegata-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Orbea variegata'' |website=Rhs.org.uk| access-date = 14 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental 
| date = July 2017 | page = 70 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 14 April 2018}}</ref>

==Distribution==
Native to [[southern Africa]], it thrives at altitudes between 0 and about 1,000 meters. It grows on gently sloping, but rarely steep, rocky [[Grade (slope)|slope]]s, sometimes under bushes, but also in locations with more or less full sun exposure.
